**Green Plate restaurants expand compost program**

Green Plate has expanded a food-scrap collection program from three restaurants to all nine of its city locations. Kitchen teams separate vegetable trimmings and coffee grounds from other waste, and a local composting company collects the material four evenings a week.

The pilot locations reduced general trash pickups by about one-third. Operations manager Pilar Santos said the biggest challenge was finding containers small enough for busy preparation areas. The chain solved that problem by testing three container shapes with kitchen staff before choosing a narrow model on wheels.

Green Plate will track collection weights for six months. If the results remain consistent, the company plans to add customer-facing compost bins at two high-volume locations.

questions.question_text: How often is compostable material collected?
The word “track” in the final paragraph is closest in meaning to
Why did Green Plate test several container shapes?

options.text: To find one suitable for limited kitchen space

questions.question_text: What may happen if the six-month results are consistent?

options.text: All general trash pickup will stop.
Kitchen staff will stop sorting food scraps.
Some restaurants will add bins for customers.

**Transfer request 7421**
Approved Monday 10:40 A.M.

Please make sure request 7421 reaches us no later than 2 P.M. Wednesday. We begin installing the cases at 3 P.M. Tuesday if they arrive by then, but Wednesday noon is still acceptable. After the route is assigned, send me its number so I can schedule the unloading crew. Do not split the load just to use an earlier truck.
